pr_title: session: add session var to update global logger max days
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #27520 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary: Currently, it is required to restart instance to change max-days of log files(log.file.max-days in config file). We want to enable user to change such config dynamically.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:
- added a session scope variable(tidb_log_file_max_days) to adjust max days of logger

How it Works:
- when user want to dynamically change max days of general log, they can change the session variable
- internally, it will create a new logger instance with new max days config to replace the global logger instance
- the session value is stored in memory, and it may inconsistent with the actual log file config. the main purpose is to provide a way to dynamically adjust the max days, but not to provide a consistent view of log file max days config

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [x] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No code

We setup and run an tidb cluster with a given max-days=30 and max-size=30 in config
```
mysql> select @@tidb_log_file_max_days;
+--------------------------+
| @@tidb_log_file_max_days |
+--------------------------+
| 30                       |
+--------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```
Enable general log
```
mysql> set tidb_general_log = 1;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)
```

```
sysbench oltp_read_write --table-size=1000000 --mysql-db=sysbench --mysql-user=root --mysql-host=127.0.0.1 --mysql-port=4000 prepare
```

Let set max days to some values and run sysbench to generate new logs, and check if logs are purged as expected(this is due to purge only happen when new logs are generated):

Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)

❯ sysbench oltp_read_write --mysql-db=sysbench --mysql-user=root --mysql-port=4000  --max-time=10 --mysql-host=127.0.0.1 run

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [x] Affects user behaviors

- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

```release-note
Add session variable tidb_log_file_max_days to dynamically adjust general log and slow log max days
```

This variable is named 'tidb_general_log_max_days' but it is not limited to the 'general log' actually. Is it a good idea to name it 'tidb_log_file_max_days'?

@bb7133 Previously, i found `newSlowQueryLogger()` doesn't change max days of slow logger, but @SabaPing is creating a PR to fix that: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/27625. Combined with these two, we can make it as `tidb_log_file_max_days `. good suggestions here!

Once the variable is set, is there any way to use `log.file.max-days` in config file 'back'? Or do we need to provide a way to do it?

/cc @morgo

> Once the variable is set, is there any way to use `log.file.max-days` in config file 'back'? Or do we need to provide a way to do it?

Because it is session scope, the `log.file.max-days` will be restored when the tidb-server is restarted. This is the same behavior as `TiDBForcePriority`, which is also configurable in config/a session sysvar.

(i.e. the behavior of `tidb_config` is static and represents the config file unchanged. If we do change it, it might not be a good thing because the user has no way of checking their config is out of sync.)

Unfortunately [libfaketime](https://github.com/wolfcw/libfaketime) doesn't work with Go, that would have made testing easier and/or more realistic. Interesting enough the golang playground etc are using a fake time ([example](https://play.golang.org/p/p_d2Lchu379)). However I think the testing here is sufficient for this PR.

In MySQL [`expire_logs_days`](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/replication-options-binary-log.html#sysvar_expire_logs_days) was [replaced by](https://dev.mysql.com/worklog/task/?id=10924) [`binlog_expire_logs_seconds`](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/replication-options-binary-log.html#sysvar_binlog_expire_logs_seconds). While this variable doesn't server the same purpose it might be good to consider settings in seconds or hours instead of days. Another option would be to allow decimal values like `0.5` days.

Another option is to leave some of this work to the OS, like `logrotate` and `journald`. Sending this to a socket is another option. Some of these might make it easier to filter, compress, forward and de-duplicate log entries, especially when using JSON. However I don't think this is in scope for this PR.

issue_context.title: expose log.file.max-days as a dynamic parameter
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

Please allow changes on `log.file.max-days` dynamically on tidb instance.

Currently it is necessary to restart the instance to apply a different `log.file.max-days` configuration. 

Although the set config won't persists, the customer would be able to change the parameters in a persistent way editing the config files (tiup with --skip-restart)

review_comments: Do we need to replace slow query logger to enable slow log runtime modification either?
